name: Glitch Kit
description: Percussion kit of twelve small digital faults: clicks, pops, cuts of noise, static, sine pips, chirps and stutters. Each key of the octave is one sound, and the octave it is played in tunes it.

params.name: Tune
params.description: Tunes the whole kit up or down: every pip, pop, sweep, buzz and click band moves with it, and higher sounds get a little shorter. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Length
params.description: How long every sound lasts, from clipped ticks to longer bursts. The spacing of the repeats stays where Density puts it. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Tone
params.description: A low-pass filter over the whole kit. Lower is duller and softer, like faults heard through a wall; all the way up is open and bright.

params.name: Edge
params.description: How hard each sound starts and stops. Low rounds every start and stop; high switches them on and off, so a click at each end becomes part of the sound.

params.name: Density
params.description: How many events the double click, the crackle and the stutter make and how close together they lie. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Crush
params.description: Lowers the bit depth and the sample rate of the whole kit, from clean to coarse, gritty steps with ringing overtones. The level stays about the same.

params.name: Scatter
params.description: How much each hit differs from the last in pitch, length, level, place and, for the noisy sounds, the pattern itself. At zero every hit of a key is identical.

params.name: Spread
params.description: How far the hits are thrown to the left and right. At zero the kit is mono; the low pop stays in the centre at any setting. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the kit. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many hits pile up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Twelve one-shot voices built from the usual faults of digital audio (impulses through a resonant band, windowed sines, gated and held noise, a pulse train, swept sines, a shift-register clock), each key of the octave one voice with two slots; shares no code with the glitch effect.
